answer.sameness: Almost every page uses the exact same bento-box grid system or a rigid 2-column split (headline on left, contact/hours table or single photo on right). A 3-photo collage (one top-right, two bottom) repeats verbatim across frizerski-salon-mia-gen, gostilna-pri-mostu-gen, kmetija-grabnar-gen, pekarna-kvas-gen, and trgovina-oljka-in-sol-regen. Another layout—a full-width top photo above a dark horizontal band with a left headline—repeats on avto-kovac-gen, elektro-zupan-regen, pizzeria-oljka-regen, vulkanizer-zorman-regen, and zobozdravstvo-lebar-gen. Mobile views all share identical sticky bottom action bars ('Klic / Navodila za pot' or 'Pokličite') and identical 'Meni' buttons.
recurringIssues: Long Slovenian words break mid-word across lines without hyphens, ruining headlines (e.g., racunovodstvo-seliskar-regen, elektro-zupan-regen, kljucavnicarstvo-hrovat-regen).
Text-only hero screens leave huge, unstyled white voids that look unfinished and uninviting (e.g., pizzeria-oljka-gen, instrukcije-pia-gen, elektro-zupan-gen).
Oversized display type gets clipped or collides with the bottom edge of the first screen (e.g., instalacije-rebernik-regen, prevajanje-kolar-gen, instrukcije-pia-regen).
Sticky bottom CTA bars on mobile cover body text, drop caps, and photos directly beneath them.
Awkward, oversized drop caps in the body copy create visual clutter and fight with the main headlines (e.g., avto-kovac-regen, fizioterapija-pregib-gen).
Boring administrative tables (address, phone, opening hours) are used as the primary visual element on the right half of the hero screen.
Several trades and service pages use landscape or vineyard photos that have nothing to do with the business (e.g., vulkanizer-zorman-gen, mizarstvo-lesnik-regen).

best.why: Warm, cohesive earth tones pair naturally with authentic bakery photography, and the typography fits the grid comfortably on both desktop and mobile.
Rich dark brown and olive palette feels genuinely tailored to an Istrian delicacies shop, with well-cropped product imagery and balanced hierarchy.
Dark moody aesthetic, sharp serif headlines, and warm photography create an authentic barbershop atmosphere that holds together well.

weakest.why: The headline font is far too large for the column, breaking 'Računovodstvo' awkwardly across lines and leaving dangling commas at the start of lines.
A pizzeria homepage with zero food photography and a vast, empty white void in the center looks like a broken wireframe.
The narrow left column forces 'ZAKLENJENI?' to break mid-word and puts a comma at the start of a line, paired with a sterile text table.

answer.oneChange: Enforce responsive typography scaling (using clamp() and proper Slovenian hyphenation/word-break rules) so long words never split mid-word without hyphens, and ban photography-free hero layouts that rely on plain text tables to fill the screen.
answer.summary: This portfolio looks like the output of an automated layout generator cycling through four rigid wireframes rather than a bespoke design studio. While the color palettes and serif/sans-serif pairings attempt to match each industry, the underlying structures are repetitive and mechanical. The biggest flaw is poor typographic control: long Slovenian words frequently snap in half without hyphens or overflow the viewport. Furthermore, several pages lack hero imagery altogether, leaving stark white voids or dull address tables where a strong visual hook should be. Fix the broken word-wrapping, eliminate the text-only hero screens, and stop relying on the exact same three-photo bento grid for every craft and food business.
